course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Trigonometric and Polar Functions
unit.description: Model periodic phenomena with sine, cosine, and tangent, use inverse trigonometric functions and identities, and describe how polar functions change.

firstTopic.title: Periodic Phenomena
firstTopic.summary: What makes a relationship periodic, how one cycle of a graph builds the whole graph, the period of a function, and estimating a period from data.

topics.title: Periodic Phenomena
topics.summary: What makes a relationship periodic, how one cycle of a graph builds the whole graph, the period of a function, and estimating a period from data.

topics.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
topics.summary: Angles in standard position, terminal rays, radian measure, and the sine, cosine, and tangent of an angle defined from a point on a circle centered at the origin.

topics.title: Sine and Cosine Function Values
topics.summary: The coordinates (r cos θ, r sin θ) of a point on a circle centered at the origin, and exact sine and cosine values for multiples of π/4 and π/6 from special right triangles.

topics.title: Sine and Cosine Function Graphs
topics.summary: The sine and cosine functions as the vertical and horizontal displacements of a point moving around the unit circle, their domains, their outputs between −1 and 1, and how to sketch their graphs.

topics.title: Sinusoidal Functions
topics.summary: Sinusoidal functions as transformations of sin θ, with period, frequency, amplitude, and midline, plus the concavity of their graphs and the symmetry that makes sine odd and cosine even.

topics.title: Sinusoidal Function Transformations
topics.summary: How a, b, c, and d in f(θ) = a sin(b(θ + c)) + d set the amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline of a sinusoidal function, for both sine and cosine.

topics.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
topics.summary: Building sinusoidal models of periodic phenomena: the period from consecutive maximums or minimums, the amplitude and midline from the extreme values, the phase shift from one data point, sinusoidal regression, and where a model can be trusted.

topics.title: The Tangent Function
topics.summary: The tangent function as the slope of the terminal ray, its period of π, its vertical asymptotes, its increasing and changing concavity between asymptotes, and its additive and multiplicative transformations.

topics.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
topics.summary: Arcsine, arccosine, and arctangent: why the trigonometric functions need restricted domains to be invertible, which domains are used, and how the output of an inverse trigonometric function is read as an angle.

topics.title: Trigonometric Equations and Inequalities
topics.summary: Solving equations and inequalities involving trigonometric functions: one solution from an inverse function, the others from symmetry and periodicity, and the domain restrictions that a context implies.

topics.title: The Secant, Cosecant, and Cotangent Functions
topics.summary: Secant, cosecant, and cotangent as reciprocals of cosine, sine, and tangent: where they are defined, their vertical asymptotes, their ranges, and the shapes of their graphs.

topics.title: Equivalent Representations of Trigonometric Functions
topics.summary: The Pythagorean identity and forms derived from it, the sum identities for sine and cosine with their difference and double-angle versions, and using equivalent forms to solve trigonometric equations.

topics.title: Trigonometry and Polar Coordinates
topics.summary: The polar coordinate system, polar coordinates (r, θ) with positive and negative r, converting between polar and rectangular coordinates, and locating complex numbers with either system.

topics.title: Polar Function Graphs
topics.summary: Graphing r = f(θ) in polar coordinates: reading angle as direction and output as signed radius, connecting the rectangular graph of r against θ to the polar curve, and restricting the domain to draw part of a curve.

topics.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
topics.summary: When the graph of a polar function moves toward or away from the origin, relative extrema as points closest to or farthest from the origin, and the average rate of change of r with respect to θ.
